script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - DAY

JAMES, 38, sits on the floor surrounded by a sea of job application forms and an overflowing trash can filled with rejection letters. He's disheveled, unshaven, and looks defeated.

JAMES (to himself)
(sighing)
Another day, another dollar...or should I say another application, another rejection.

James' phone rings. He answers, excited.

JAMES
(smiling)
Hi, this is James.

INT. EMPLOYMENT AGENCY - DAY

AGENT SARAH, 28, a friendly, ambitious woman, sits at her desk with a stack of applications. She looks up as she hears James' voice over the phone.

AGENT SARAH
(smiling)
Hi, James. I've reviewed your application, and I think you could be a great fit for our team.

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - DAY

James jumps up from the floor, ecstatic.

JAMES
(grinning)
Really? That's amazing news! What kind of work would it be?

INT. EMPLOYMENT AGENCY - DAY

Agent Sarah looks at James' file.

AGENT SARAH
We're looking for a customer service representative. It's a call center position, but there's potential for growth, and you'll be part of a great team.

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - DAY

James grins, knowing this is his chance.

JAMES
(determined)
I'll take it. When do I start?

INT. EMPLOYMENT AGENCY - TRAINING ROOM - DAY

James attends a customer service training session. He's nervous, but excited to learn new skills. He makes friends with his fellow trainees and listens intently to their instructor.

TRAINER
(encouraging)
Remember, every interaction with a customer is an opportunity to make a difference in their day. Be patient, kind, and understanding.

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James practices role-playing scenarios with his reflection in the mirror, working to perfect his customer service skills. He puts on a smile and repeats the trainer's words.

JAMES
(practicing)
Hello, this is James speaking. How may I assist you today?

INT. CALL CENTER - DAY

James starts his first day at the call center, feeling both anxious and proud. His colleagues greet him warmly, and he settles into his new role.

INT. CALL CENTER - WEEKS LATER

James has mastered the art of customer service. He's received multiple praise from his supervisor and has gained the respect of his colleagues. He's proud of his new career and the progress he's made.

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James sits on the couch, looking at his reflection in the TV. He's no longer the defeated man from before. He's a customer service representative who has found a new sense of purpose.

JAMES
(smiling)
Another day, another dollar...this time, it's worth it.

FADE OUT.
